blocks.text: HOARDING CLEANOUT FAQ
Hoarding Cleanouts in Uxbridge — Honest Answers to Common Questions

items.q: What's the cost to clean out a hoarder's house in Uxbridge?
a: Hoarder clean out cost depends on the volume of belongings, the number of rooms or buildings affected, and how much sorting is involved — a single room prices modestly, a full property with a barn or shed costs more given the time required. The exact figure is confirmed free at a private walkthrough, with no township or distance premium anywhere.

items.q: Do you charge extra for rural properties or long laneways?
a: Never. The same flat pricing applies at a Brock Street home and at the end of a concession laneway — no distance fee, no rural markup, no exceptions.

items.q: What's the best way to clean out a hoarder's house?
a: Professional help, a clear plan, and patience. Going in without a strategy usually causes more distress than progress. The most effective approach sorts systematically — keep, donate, recycle, dispose — respects the resident’s input wherever they’re able to give it, and moves at a pace the household can handle, sometimes across more than one visit.

items.q: Can the cleanout include a barn or outbuilding, not just the house?
a: Yes — it’s regular work for us on Uxbridge’s farm properties. Multiple structures get scoped and quoted together, and materials or tools worth keeping are sorted with a careful eye rather than treated as simple waste.

items.q: Do you cover the hamlets — Goodwood, Zephyr, Leaskdale, Sandford?
a: Every one, at the same flat pricing as downtown. No address waits longer or pays more, ever.

items.q: Can the cleanout happen while the person continues living in the home?
a: Yes, and it’s one of the most common ways a hoarding cleanout actually happens. Work can proceed room by room while the resident stays in the home throughout.

items.q: What happens if we find valuables, documents or sentimental items?
a: They’re set aside immediately and brought to the family or resident, never sorted into a donation or disposal pile by default.

items.q: What if the property has safety hazards — pests, mould, structural damage?
a: Those get flagged honestly. Live Junk Free doesn’t disturb suspected biohazards or structural issues — the concern is identified and the household is pointed toward the right licensed specialist before the rest of the cleanout proceeds.

items.q: Why choose Live Junk Free over a general junk removal company for this?
a: Experience and approach. A hoarding cleanout calls for patience, discretion and a crew that’s done this kind of work often enough to handle it calmly, whatever the household or the property.
